To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we characterize the learning of a Gaussian mixture model via the empirical risk minimization (ERM) estimator in high-dimensional settings, and that we show that the ERM estimator can be efficiently computed for a mixture with sparsity constraints and for max-margin classification problems.

1) Gaussian mixtures are a powerful model to describe the behaviour of multi-class classification tasks, even for high dimensional data sets; 2) The ERM estimator is a consistent estimator of the underlying model; 3) The ERM learning curve is well described by a Gaussian mixture model; 4) The ERM solution is a consistent estimator in the high-dimensional regime; 5) The ERM loss can be used to infer the underlying model parameters.
